points.point: The Vault's radar-specific instrument is the AREG800A automotive radar echo generator, not a signaling tester.
points.label: covered
points.why: states AREG800A is for radar echo/target simulation and not the signaling tester role

points.point: Radar in the Vault's defense/counter-UAV context is only a detection sensor category with no test method or product detail.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not mention defense/counter-UAV radar is only a sensor category with no method/product detail

points.point: In the device testing value chain, signaling testers (CMX500/CMW500) occupy the signaling / protocol / application layer.
points.label: covered
points.why: places CMX500/CMW-class tools in cellular/WLAN signaling, protocol, application-style link validation

points.point: Non-signaling testers (CMP180/CMP200/CMW100) are mapped to the production / manufacturing stage.
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions non-signaling RF checks/workflow but not the CMP180/CMP200/CMW100 production/manufacturing mapping

points.point: The CMP180 is explicitly characterized as a production / R&D non-signaling tester.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not identify CMP180 as a production/R&D non-signaling tester

points.point: In the defense (A&D) private-5G resilience work the signaling tester is used as the 5G network emulator for the communications link, not for radar.
points.label: partial
points.why: places CMX500 on communications links, but does not specifically cover the A&D private-5G resilience/smart-jamming setup

points.point: On air vehicles the signaling tester's role is link signaling plus multi-technology de-sense validation across co-located radios.
points.label: covered
points.why: states UAV LTE/5G/Wi-Fi signaling and multi-technology desense validation

points.point: The Vault forbids inferring a signaling tester into the EMC/EME (system-level defense) test domain or the reverse.
points.label: covered
points.why: says not to use signaling/non-signaling tester as primary radar instrument and separates it from radar/EME-style roles

invented: SMW200A configuration guide lists R&S®SMW-K78 as Radar echo generation
SMB100B pulse train option R&S®SMBB-K27 is described for radar applications
MVG is described as providing antenna characterization, radar signature evaluation, and electromagnetic measurements test solutions
